acceptance_scope: The explicit W5-VERIFY criteria and current task restrictions supersede conflicting recommendations in the original audit.

evidence: crates/jmax-syntax/src/feed.rs:270: block_at selects dispatch using total input length and classifies original slices of at most 64 bytes.
crates/jmax-syntax/src/feed.rs:75: whitespace masks use trailing_zeros; quote, escape, delimiter and digit paths also walk masks.
crates/jmax-syntax/src/lib.rs:116: complete input retains Payload; incremental input alone uses a byte vector.
crates/jmax-cursor/src/walk.rs:13: cursor and syntax share Payload owners; next and subtree skipping consume the same syntax scanner.
crates/jmax-cursor/src/resume.rs:29: finalization moves original payload and decoded storage.
crates/jmax-dispatch/Cargo.toml: std forwards to scalar, NEON, AVX2 and AVX-512 scanners.
PERF-01.verification_repair: Added syntax/std to dispatch/std and cursor/std to syntax/std feature propagation.
PERF-01.api_note: The concrete API is jmax_dispatch::dispatch followed by Dispatch::classify, not a free classify_block function. SIMD availability is target- and policy-dependent.

PERF-02.evidence: crates/jmax-syntax/src/frames.rs:13: per-depth generation-tagged hash/span tables use geometric growth and at most one-half load; raw or decoded bytes are compared only on matching 64-bit hashes.
PERF-02.complexity: Expected amortized O(1) in object key count, plus key bytes and hash-collision comparisons. Not worst-case constant time.

PERF-03.evidence: crates/jsonmax/src/parse.rs:26 delegates to parse_with_numeric with no post-parse DOM pass. crates/jmax-syntax/src/feed.rs:344 lexes each completed number before emission and applies supplied conversion policy to decimal/exponent tokens.
PERF-03.verification_repair: Implemented the missing numeric-aware cursor and syntax constructors instead of dropping the policy argument.

evidence: crates/jmax-schema-compile/src/keys.rs:415: lookup does not call table validation; SWAR has at most eight candidates and hashing has bounded probes.
crates/jmax-schema-compile/src/image.rs:864: validation constructs immutable program indexes once.
crates/jmax-schema-vm/src/objects.rs:78: lookup_index returns a global key index, converted by subtraction to the local seen-bit index.
crates/jmax-schema-vm/src/objects.rs:198: slot_for_field replaces slot scans; table_state replaces owner scans.
PERF-04.complexity: Known-key and slot lookup are constant in table size, plus hashing and comparing query-key bytes. Required-field checks at object completion remain linear once per object; defensive unknown-key duplicate tracking is separate.

PERF-05.evidence: crates/jmax-encode/src/writer.rs:308 uses SIMD-capable escape discovery and bulk safe-run writes. crates/jsonmax/src/encode.rs returns trusted typed and DOM output without full-output reparsing.
PERF-05.qualification: DOM number emission retains local fragment validation; trusted JsonEncode implementations must honor their JSON contract.

evidence: crates/jmax-bench/src/parse.rs:135 invokes extract_payload with the retained CompiledSchema and Selection.
Full DOM and slot digests are computed before measure; timed result consumption uses fixed-size summaries and black_box.
crates/jmax-bench/src/serialize.rs:132 computes corpus retention during preparation; each timed document emission adds sink capacity in O(1).
crates/jmax-bench/src/bin/jmax_bench.rs covers seven workloads and Parse, Validate, Extract and Serialize; output includes decimal MB/s, ns/op and messages per second.
PERF-06.verification_repair: Added ns/op as total elapsed nanoseconds divided by total measured documents, with zero guards.
PERF-06.scope_override: No external comparison baseline was added because this task explicitly forbids that dependency.

contracts: jmax_dom::Document = jmax_abi::node::ValidatedDocument; jsonmax::Document re-exports the same type.
JM-01.evidence: ABI accessors, DOM builders, facade parsing/encoding and benchmark parse/serialize consumers use identical types. DocumentMetadata::get consumes the borrowed view and returns a document-lifetime reference, supporting temporary metadata views.

JM-02.evidence: Facade compile_graph retains Arc<ValidatedProgram>. Request validation never loads an image or recompiles a schema. The facade load API recompiles source once and compares the exact retained image.

JM-03.evidence: ValidatedProgram shares complete CompiledProgram and ProgramIndexes. CompiledSchema retains the witness through Arc and exposes program() -> &ValidatedProgram. Workload has compiled_schema: jsonmax::endpoint::CompiledSchema, populated by corpus construction and borrowed by parse operations.

JM-04.evidence: crates/jsonmax/src/endpoint.rs:337 passes program, an owned Payload-based adapter, selection, then VmLimits, exactly matching the callee. VM execution obtains decoded bytes after each event, permits append-only arena reallocation, validates final owners, and publishes after strict EOF.

JM-05.evidence: Facade manifest includes jmax-schema-ir. Benchmark manifest includes jmax-dom, jmax-dispatch and jmax-schema-ir. The std-gated binary target is jmax_bench at src/bin/jmax_bench.rs.

JM-06.evidence: crates/jmax-bench/src/serialize.rs:175 calls an associated function without a mutable receiver, borrowing documents[index] immutably and sink mutably as disjoint fields.

JM-07.evidence: crates/jmax-utf8/src/validate.rs uses simdutf8::compat::from_utf8. The local optional dependency's Cargo manifest declares library name simdutf8. Both feature branches preserve UTF-8 error offsets.

evidence: Requests accept numeric u32 method IDs and normalize them for dispatch, including untagged method/seq/params requests.
Immediate supports method, seq and params; aliases data/result remain accepted.
Stream supports original_seq, method, stream_seq, stream_code and data with independent method and topic identifiers.
Error supports u32 status code, numeric method, seq, string log_id and arbitrary params; the signed legacy decoder extension remains accepted.
EndpointLibsResponse and responses::encode_endpoint_libs expose exact fields for all six canonical response variants.
OwnedEnvelope exposes method_code(), stream_seq() and stream_code(); view.seq normalizes original_seq and view.result_span normalizes data or Immediate params.
dispatch::resolve_route_with_role_ids and RequestContext accept u32 roles; ABI string metadata can contain decimal role IDs.
Presence masks are now u32 for all 18 envelope fields.

house_rule_cleanup.evidence: Source searches over crate Rust files and manifests returned no prohibited inline test attributes, stubs, runtime/thread imports, comparison dependency or em-dash characters.

integration_mismatches_fixed: DOM parse_with_numeric and facade validate_syntax called a nonexistent cursor constructor; added the exact four-argument API and propagated policy into syntax scanning.
Standalone syntax/cursor std features did not activate runtime SIMD dispatch; completed the feature chain.
Wire presence masks used 16 bits for 18 fields; widened masks and shifts to u32.
Tagged response decoder and encoder disagreed with the local endpoint-libs fields; aligned Immediate, Stream, Error, Log, Forwarded and Close and added an exact canonical response API.
Tagged error code decoding treated status as endpoint ID; separated method routing from u32 status validation and retained the signed extension.
CLI lacked the audit's ns/op metric; added it without executing the binary.
qualifications: No compilation, execution, benchmark result or measured speedup is claimed.

The number crate's lexer remains scalar and float conversion delegates to core decimal parsing. An Eisel-Lemire or SWAR numeric implementation is not claimed; the requested redundant DOM number scan is removed.
The original external comparison-baseline recommendation is superseded by this task's explicit dependency prohibition.
NumberArray and Nested use empty strict selections under the current object-property slot model, while validating the full document.

Existing native Response lacks separate method/topic IDs and log IDs. Its dialect conversion reuses the code for both stream identifiers and supplies empty/zero log IDs. EndpointLibsResponse preserves exact distinct values. Missing required native identifiers and out-of-range u32 conversions fail before emission.
Known-key schema lookup is bounded; defensive unknown-key duplicate tracking remains separate from indexed schema lookup.
